study type: Secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
exposure: Outpatient cervical ripening with a Foley catheter
Inpatient cervical ripening with a Foley catheter
outcome: Time from labor and delivery (L&D) admission to delivery
Time from admission to hospital discharge
Rates of clinically diagnosed chorioamnionitis and endometritis
cohort: Nulliparous patients undergoing elective induction of labor (eIOL)
finding: Outpatient cervical ripening with a Foley catheter was associated with a shorter time from labor and delivery admission to delivery, shorter total hospital stay, and decreased cesarean delivery rate in nulliparous patients with BMI ≥ 30 kg/m(2) undergoing elective induction of labor.
